I have thorough, verified coverage. Writing the report now.

# 13 — Prior-Art Synthesis: The Chorizite Evaluation + Hook Inventory

## 0. Executive summary

Two separate "should we retarget to another host?" studies exist in these checkouts, and they reach the *same* structural conclusion from opposite ends:

- **RynthCore's Chorizite study** (`rynthsuite/Docs/Chorizite_*.md`, dated 2026-05-06) was **not** a plan to run RynthAi *on* Chorizite. It was a **mining survey**: harvest hooks/assets from Chorizite into RynthCore, which itself still detours retail `acclient.exe`. Conclusion: "we are mostly ahead; adopt a short list." Nothing was killed; the "gaps" are *adoption caveats* (NativeAOT vs. AssemblyLoadContext, VA drift, `List.cs` crashes, `DatReaderWriter` NativeAOT unknown).
- **holtburger's own Chorizite study** (`apps/holtburger-web/CHORIZITE_PORTING_PLAN.md`, Rev 3) reached the harder verdict: **most of Chorizite is un-portable to the browser** because it is DLL-injection-with-hardcoded-memory-offsets into retail `acclient.exe` — but its high-level API/data model, enums, dat fixtures, and manifest model are valuable.

The load-bearing insight for our RynthAi→holtburger-web integration: **Chorizite's entire hook inventory (and RynthCore's) is machinery for observing a binary you do not control. holtburger-web *is* the client, so the whole class of hook-fragility problems evaporates — and holtburger has *already reimplemented*, from the same retail decompile Chorizite reverse-engineered by hand, nearly every behavior those hooks exposed.** The gaps are overwhelmingly **CLOSED** or **MOOT**, not inherited.

---

## (a) What the Rynth authors concluded — in their own cited words

### The framing (this was a mining survey, not a host swap)
`Chorizite_Hook_Gap_Analysis.md:6`: *"The aim is to identify Chorizite hooks we could adopt and to record where we have already surpassed Chorizite, so we don't waste cycles re-deriving things they've already mapped."* The companion asset audit covers *"everything else they have that we could utilize"* (`Chorizite_NonHook_Asset_Audit.md:7`). Neither doc proposes running RynthAi inside Chorizite; both treat Chorizite as a **parts donor** for a RynthCore that keeps hooking retail acclient.

### The hook gaps they found (things Chorizite has, RynthCore lacked)
All addresses assume the `0x00400000` retail build (`Hook_Gap_Analysis.md:8`).

| Tier | Hook (Chorizite VA) | Exposes | Their verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tooltip start/reset/check `0x0045DF70`/`0x0045C440`/`0x0045B7C0` | hovered object+icon, per-frame eval | adopt — appraisal-on-hover w/o polling (`:16-20,29`) |
| 1 | Drag start `0x0045E120` / Drop `0x00461860` | item/spell id, drop target | adopt — inventory tooling (`:22-23,29`) |
| 1 | Cursor `0x0045A910` | cursor + hotspot | adopt — overlay cursor-awareness (`:23,30`) |
| 1 | Floaty lock `0x004D3C20` | compass/radar lock state | adopt — ties to RynthRadar (`:24,31`) |
| 2 | `UIFlow::UseNewMode` `0x00479AA0` | charsel↔login↔world transitions | **top priority** (`:37,81`) |
| 2 | `Client::Cleanup` `0x004118D0` | pre-teardown | defensive, logout-crash class (`:38,84`) |
| 3 | socket `SendTo`/`RecvFrom`, dat I/O, `SetSelectedObject` | — | **skip** (`:44-47`) |

### What "killed/stalled" the naive port (the operative caveats)
The docs record no project death — they record **blockers to adoption**, quoted:

- **Runtime-model conflict:** *"Chorizite's design assumes per-plugin AssemblyLoadContext isolation, which conflicts with our NativeAOT model and may not be portable directly"* (`Asset_Audit.md:48`); *"we cannot adopt the AssemblyLoadContext mechanism wholesale"* (`:118`).
- **Version/VA drift is the recurring killer:** *"VAs and struct offsets … should be validated against our running client"* (`:9`); the open question *"VA drift over time on `master` is the main risk"* (`:158`).
- **Their own fixtures crash the client:** *"`List.cs` — memory `feedback_idlist_vas.md` confirms its IDList VAs crash our client; use Weenie.cs equivalents. Other VAs in `List.cs` likely also unreliable"* (`:132`).
- **Toolchain unknowns:** *"Does `DatReaderWriter` support NativeAOT x86? Verify before §1.2/§3.2"* (`:156`).

### holtburger's sharper verdict on why the whole thing doesn't cross to web
`CHORIZITE_PORTING_PLAN.md` §0: *"Most of Chorizite is **not directly portable**. It's a C# plugin ecosystem that runs inside the retail `acclient.exe` process via DLL injection (`Chorizite.Injector`), with bindings (`ACBindings`) that are literal hardcoded memory offsets into the running game (e.g. `0x0051AEA0`). You cannot drop that into a Rust + WASM + Three.js browser client."* Its "Critical reframe #2": the real oracle is *"the local `~/ac-headers/` directory … the full Hex-Rays decompiled source of retail `acclient.exe` (`acclient.c`, 938k lines)"* — **the same retail decompile RynthCore's hook work anchors on.**

## (b) Which gaps holtburger-web CLOSES vs. INHERITS

Verdict key: **CLOSED** = native equivalent verified in source · **MOOT** = gap is an artifact of the inject-into-acclient architecture and does not exist for a from-scratch web client · **PARTIAL/INHERITED** = feature area exists but the specific signal still needs building.

### Hook gaps (from `Chorizite_Hook_Gap_Analysis.md`)

| Chorizite hook | holtburger-web equivalent (verified) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Tooltip (start/reset/check) | `plugins/hover-tooltip.js` (+`.manifest.json`); appraisal event `CLIENT_EVENT_KIND_OBJECT_APPRAISED = 32` at `src/lib.rs:21146-21164` explicitly *"closes matrix row 12 (`Item_SetAppraiseInfo`)"*; `GameAction::IdentifyObject` `lib.rs:21698` | **CLOSED** |
| Drag start / Drop | DOM drag-drop: `plugins/container-panel.js:338-390` (`slot.draggable`, `dragstart`/`dragover`/`drop` → `moveItem`); `plugins/spellbook.js:1242-1247` (`row.draggable`, `application/x-hb-spell-id` mime); backed by `SessionHandle::move_item` `lib.rs:54436`, `put_item_in_container` `:54457`, `drop_item` `:33594` | **CLOSED** |
| Cursor change | DOM/CSS cursor is native to the browser (no memory hook needed) | **CLOSED (trivial)** |
| Floaty lock (compass/radar lock state) | `plugins/radar.js`, `plugins/examine-floaty.js` (`gmFloatyExaminationUI 0x2100006B`), `plugins/examine-target.js` exist; the specific *"locked"* state signal not verified | **PARTIAL** |
| `UIFlow::UseNewMode` (screen-mode transitions) | `index.html:5145-5185` — native `window.__bootState` state machine + `holtburger:state` CustomEvent; explicit sequence `init→form-shown→connecting→kicking→reconnecting→char-list-ready→spawning→in-world` (`:5160-5162`), designed to *"replace… the polling pattern many plugins use"* (`:1420`) | **CLOSED (cleaner)** |
| `Client::Cleanup` (pre-teardown) | wasm/JS owns its own lifecycle; kick-reconnect-logout dance is scripted (`index.html:5153-5158`), `error` is a first-class boot state | **CLOSED (owns lifecycle)** |

The four "we're already ahead of Chorizite" hook families RynthCore listed (`Hook_Gap_Analysis.md:55-62` — combat mode, object lifecycle, login/logout, selected-target) are **also native in holtburger** and reachable poll-style: `toggle_combat_mode`/`set_combat_mode`/`get_suggested_combat_mode` (`lib.rs:32372,32391`, opcode `ChangeCombatMode 0x0053` at `opcodes.rs:532`); target/selection (`select_character` `lib.rs:31696`, `target_id` `:24792`, `target_cycle.js`); chat (`send_chat`/`send_tell`/`send_channel`/`send_turbine_channel`/`send_emote` `lib.rs:31796-31892`); login-complete (`opcodes.rs:479 LoginComplete = 0x00A1`, `CharacterList = 0xF658` `:21`).

### Non-hook assets (from `Chorizite_NonHook_Asset_Audit.md`)

| Chorizite asset (their §) | holtburger-web equivalent (verified) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Dat reader — `FSDatReader.cs` + `DatReaderWriter` NuGet; SpellTable/SpellComponentTable/SkillTable/VitalTable (§1.2) | **`crates/holtburger-dat`, 56 `file_type/` parsers**, incl. `spell_table.rs` (964 L), `skill_table.rs` (194 L), `spell_components_table.rs` (194 L), `xp_table.rs`, `combat_maneuver_table.rs`, `motion_table.rs`, etc. Native Rust; compiles to wasm | **CLOSED (more complete)** — and it dissolves their open Q "does `DatReaderWriter` support NativeAOT x86?" (`:156`) |
| Frustum + BoundingBox (§1.3, "port verbatim") | `scene3d/culling.js:123-187` `FrustumCuller` → `new THREE.Frustum()`, `setFromProjectionMatrix`, `intersectsSphere`/`Box3` | **CLOSED (three.js built-in)** |
| Plugin manifest — Id/Name/Version/**Dependencies**/**Environments** (§1.4) | `plugins/schemas/plugin-manifest.json`: `required:["id","name","version"]` (`:7`), `dependencies` (`:53`), `environments` (`:63`), `slots` (`:77`); live example `examine-floaty.manifest.json` carries `"environments":["browser"]` | **CLOSED (both wanted fields present)** |
| NetworkParser — opcode dispatch (§2.3) | `crates/holtburger-protocol/src/opcodes.rs` (1049 L) + `messages/` (chat, combat, magic, trade, inventory, movement…). Opcode-level, not socket-level — same advantage RynthCore claimed over Chorizite | **CLOSED** |
| Backend event-arg types — ChatInput/ShowTooltip/DragDrop/UILocked (§2.1, "design references") | native typed client-event surface (`CLIENT_EVENT_KIND_*` in `lib.rs`) + `scene3d/client_event_dispatch.js`, `entity_dispatch.js` | **CLOSED (were reference-only anyway)** |
| AcClient struct layouts — Inventory/Movement/Physics/Magic/Combat/Net/Player.cs = memory offsets (§2.2) | holtburger owns wire types in `holtburger-protocol/messages/*`; no in-process structs to lay out. Their warning that `List.cs` VAs *"crash our client"* (`:132`) is inapplicable | **MOOT (owns protocol types)** |
| Render abstractions — BaseRenderer/DrawList/FontManager… (§2.4, "too coupled to copy") | three.js r184 + EffectComposer (`scene3d/`) | **CLOSED (own renderer)** |
| SymbolResolver / crash enrichment — `acclient.map` RVA→symbol at native AV (§1.1) | no native AV in wasm; `console_error_panic_hook::set_once()` `lib.rs:871` + source maps is the analog | **MOOT (different crash model)** |
| FileWatcher — `FileSystemWatcher` debounce for hot-reload (§1.5) | browser sandbox cannot watch the filesystem; service-worker cache + `?nosw=1` fill the reload role | **MOOT (N/A on web)** |

**Net:** of the 6 hook families → 5 CLOSED, 1 PARTIAL, 0 truly inherited. Of the ~9 asset families → 5 CLOSED, 3 MOOT-by-architecture, 1 CLOSED-was-reference. **holtburger-web closes essentially the entire Chorizite gap list**, mostly by construction, because it re-derives behavior from the retail decompile instead of hooking the retail binary.

## (c) Transferable lessons for the RynthAi→holtburger-web integration

1. **Hooks don't port; behaviors do.** Chorizite's and RynthCore's entire hook inventories are apparatus for *observing a binary you don't own*. Every fragility they log — *"its function RVAs do not always line up with the user's live client binary … implement… with pattern scanning rather than fixed addresses"* (`ACCLIENT_HOOK_INVENTORY.md:90-91`), VA drift on `master` (`Asset_Audit.md:158`), `List.cs` crashing the client (`:132`) — **has no analog in holtburger-web.** RynthAi's 344 `Has*` capability guards + poll-style `RynthCoreHost` map onto holtburger's poll-style JS globals (`entityMap`, `__diag`, `__sessionHandle`, `__bootState`) and `SessionHandle` methods, *not* onto detours. This is the strongest argument for the web target.

2. **The retail decompile is the shared Rosetta stone.** Both worlds anchor on the same artifact: RynthCore's rule *"Use the decompile to understand semantics… use the live `acclient.exe`… for hook placement"* (`ACCLIENT_HOOK_INVENTORY.md:15-18`); holtburger's *"grep `acclient.c` FIRST"* (`PORTING_PLAN §0`) and `scene3d/target_cycle.js:4-16` reimplementing `CPlayerSystem::SelectNext (acclient.c:397944)` / `UI_SELECTION_TYPE (acclient.h:3041)`. **Methodology for us:** where RynthAi's brain expects a client behavior, locate it in `acclient.c`, then confirm holtburger already reimplements it (it usually does) — the decompile is how you prove the two ends agree.

3. **Don't re-derive what's already mapped — now pointed at holtburger.** Their guiding rule (`Hook_Gap_Analysis.md:6`) applies recursively: the 56 dat parsers, the 1049-line opcode table, target-cycle math, appraisal events, combat-mode toggles, and the plugin-manifest schema are **done**. Integration work is *wiring RynthAi onto existing holtburger surfaces*, not rebuilding them.

4. **Sequence the readiness gate first.** RynthCore's top pick was `UseNewMode` as *"the central authority for 'is it safe to dereference cached AC pointers'"* (`Hook_Gap_Analysis.md:37,81`). holtburger already shipped that authority as `__bootState` + the `holtburger:state` event. **Adopt the same discipline the docs earned through login-crash debugging:** gate every RynthAi state read/action on `__bootState === 'in-world'` (and entityMap readiness). This is the concrete mitigation for the poll-vs-async inversion flagged as the deepest structural risk — `__bootState` *is* our `UseNewMode`.

5. **Follow their implementation ordering.** RynthCore's waves (`ACCLIENT_HOOK_INVENTORY.md:81-86`: lifecycle/UI → chat → world/object → combat/trade → host-API) and holtburger's "first three bricks" (`PORTING_PLAN §0`: event taxonomy → WorldObject types → **enum/opcode parity**) converge on: lifecycle & object flow before combat/trade. Port the RynthCoreHost contract in that order.

6. **What they wished they'd had — enum/opcode parity validation.** holtburger's Tier-4 lesson is to *cross-check enum integer values and opcodes* (`PORTING_PLAN §0` Tier 4). **Before wiring RynthAi, diff its property/opcode enums against `holtburger-common::properties` + `holtburger-protocol/opcodes.rs`** — a silent enum mismatch is the exact bug class both projects kept hitting.

7. **Version drift moves, it doesn't vanish.** holtburger removes *binary-VA* drift but adds a new axis: ACE-server protocol version × holtburger build version. Carry forward the docs' habit of an *"explicit unsupported-state log/UI message"* per capability (`ACCLIENT_HOOK_INVENTORY.md:24`) — it's what RynthAi's `Has*` guards already expect.

## (d) Legal / clean-room constraints that bind how we port

`LEGAL_COMPATIBILITY.md` is *"a project policy note, not legal advice"* (`:5`). The operative rules, quoted, and how each binds the port:

**What we MUST reimplement (never copy):**
- *"We do not decompile, disassemble, patch, or copy code from Decal, VTank, or any other closed plugin."* (`:11`)
- *"Do not copy source, headers, resources, strings, or assets from closed plugins."* (`:26`)
- *"If a compatibility task would require inspecting closed-source plugin internals, stop and reassess before proceeding."* (`:30`)
- Rationale: *"VTank publishes a license agreement that forbids reverse engineering, decompiling, disassembling, and redistribution"* (`:19`); the `17 U.S.C. 1201(f)` interop exception is to be treated *"as a narrow backstop instead of the core project strategy"* (`:20`).

**What we MAY copy / use (explicitly allowed):**
- *"We may build compatibility with publicly documented or behaviorally observed plugin interfaces."* (`:9`)
- *"We may use the AC client decompile and runtime behavior to locate safe host-side hook points in `acclient.exe`."* (`:10`)
- Allowed sources: *"The AC client decompile and the running AC client itself. RynthCore code and user-provided test plugins."* (`:34-36`)
- `PLUGIN_HOOK_MATRIX.md:1`: *"clean-room hook targets that can be implemented from the AC client decompile without inspecting third-party plugin binaries."*

**Preference rules that steer the design:**
- *"Prefer source/API compatibility over binary cloning."* (`:28`)
- *"Prefer RynthCore-native plugins over legacy binary compatibility whenever possible."* (`:29`)
- *"Revisit optional binary compatibility only if it stays within the guardrails in `docs/LEGAL_COMPATIBILITY.md`."* (`PLUGIN_HOOK_MATRIX.md:51`)

### How these bind our specific integration

| Situation | Ruling |
|---|---|
| Reimplementing `RynthCoreHost`'s one-class contract (the established seam) onto holtburger `SessionHandle` | **Allowed.** It is *our own* SDK code (`RynthCore code` is an allowed source, `:36`); a clean-room re-expression of our own host contract is not a closed-plugin copy. |
| holtburger deriving retail behavior from `~/ac-headers/acclient.c` (dat parsers, `SelectNext`, etc.) | **Sanctioned by the same rule** — the AC client decompile is an explicitly allowed source (`:10,35`). The web target sits inside the guardrails exactly like RynthCore's hook work does. |
| RynthAi's unportable memory-offset islands (`FellowshipTracker` hardcoded addresses; `ExpressionEngine.cs:2971` `Marshal.ReadInt64` game clock; `DungeonMapTexture` D3D9 vtable) | **Reimplement from holtburger's owned state — do not port the offsets.** This is precisely the *"binary cloning"* the policy says to avoid (`:28`); reading acclient memory offsets is a version-fragile pattern with no legal upside and no wasm target. |
| Any RynthAi surface historically shaped around Decal/VTank | **Interface-compat is fine, binary/internals are not** (`:9` vs `:11,26`). Since we re-express on holtburger's own protocol, we stay clear as long as no closed-plugin code/strings/assets are copied. |

**Bottom line for legal:** the web port is the *safest* option under this policy, not merely an acceptable one. It replaces binary-compatibility-with-a-closed-client (the thing the guardrails circle warily, `PLUGIN_HOOK_MATRIX.md:51`) with *source/API compatibility against our own protocol reimplementation derived from an explicitly-allowed decompile* — the exact preference order the policy states (`:28-29`).
